The Gaussian graphical model (GGM) is a Markov Random Field for continuous
variables. In bgms, the GGM is fit when `variable_type = "continuous"`.

## The model

A GGM assumes that $p$ continuous variables follow a multivariate normal
distribution:

$$
\mathbf{x} \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma})
$$

The network structure is encoded in the precision matrix
$\boldsymbol{K} = \boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{-1}$. A zero entry $K_{ij} = 0$
means that variables $i$ and $j$ are conditionally independent given all
other variables — equivalently, the edge between nodes $i$ and $j$ is
absent.

## Partial associations

As described in [Graphical Models](graphical-models.qmd), bgms reports all
pairwise effects on a unified partial association scale. For the GGM, the
partial association between variables $i$ and $j$ is:

$$
\phi_{ij} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\, K_{ij}
$$

This is a linear rescaling of the precision off-diagonal. A positive
$\phi_{ij}$ means that, holding all other variables constant, higher values
of $x_i$ are associated with higher values of $x_j$.

The standardized version of the precision off-diagonal gives the partial
correlation:

$$
\rho_{ij \cdot \text{rest}} = -\frac{K_{ij}}{\sqrt{K_{ii} K_{jj}}}
$$

## Fitting a GGM

To fit a GGM, pass continuous data and set `variable_type`:

```r
fit = bgm(x = continuous_data, variable_type = "continuous", seed = 1234)
```

The `summary()` and `coef()` methods work the same as for ordinal models.
`coef(fit)$pairwise` returns the partial associations $\phi_{ij}$.

To obtain model-specific parameterizations, use the dedicated extractors:

- `extract_precision(fit)` — returns the full precision matrix $\boldsymbol{K}$.
- `extract_partial_correlations(fit)` — returns the partial correlation matrix.

## Edge selection

When `edge_selection = TRUE` (the default), bgms applies spike-and-slab
priors to the partial associations $\phi_{ij}$. Edges with posterior
inclusion probability above 0.5 have more evidence for presence than
absence. See [Edge Selection](edge-selection.qmd) for details.

## Missing data

For continuous data, missing values can be imputed within the MCMC sampler
by setting `na_action = "impute"`. Missing entries are resampled at each
iteration from their full conditional distribution. The default behavior is
`na_action = "listwise"`, which removes rows with any missing values before
fitting.
